issues.legal_issue: An advertised estimated price in a self-financing commercial scheme does not by itself fix the final price, but any final price must be proportionate to the estimate and supported by relevant cost evidence.
material_facts: A commercial complex was offered under a self-financing scheme, with the advertised cost for a showroom described as an estimate in one advertisement.
After obtaining approvals and tenders, the developer calculated a substantially higher actual cost and asked contributors to agree to it, offering an option to withdraw with interest.
The application conditions stated that the listed cost was estimated and that any increase would be communicated.
The developer had not placed the relevant costing documents before the trial court.
issues.conclusion: The estimated amount did not establish an automatic right to purchase at a fixed price, nor did the developer have an absolute right to increase the price. The final cost must be proportionate to the estimate, taking account of inflation and increases in input, construction-material and labour costs, on the basis of evidence at the final hearing.
issues.legal_principle: In a self-financing scheme, the price is generally based on construction cost, and a contributor cannot claim a price below actual construction cost. However, a development authority has no absolute right to increase an estimated cost: the final cost must be proportionate to the estimate and justified by relevant evidence. Indore Development Authority v. Sadhana Agarwal (1995) 3 SCC 1 supports this approach. Kanpur Development Authority v. Sheela Devi, AIR 2004 SC 400, was distinguished because it involved an express limit on escalation and residential houses rather than a commercial complex under a self-financing scheme.

predicates.self_financing_commercial_scheme: The development was a commercial scheme in which contributors funded the construction cost of their units.
predicates.advertised_cost_was_estimated: The advertised amount was presented as an estimate rather than an unconditional fixed price.
predicates.unit_price_depended_on_construction_cost: The price of each unit was determined by the cost of constructing the scheme.

issues.definition: When a commercial scheme is self-financed, its advertised cost is estimated, and unit prices depend on construction costs, the final price must be proportionate to the estimate and supported by cost evidence.

issues.legal_issue: An interim injunction affecting a self-financing project may be set aside where it restricts project funding and the court granting it has not considered relevant costing factors and evidence.
material_facts: The trial court restrained the developer from allotting the showroom to anyone else and permitted the contributor to deposit the advertised amount in instalments.

The actual cost demanded was substantially higher than the advertised estimate, and the developer said the scheme’s costs included matters such as land, lease rent, electricity-related charges, construction inputs and financing.

The developer had not placed the relevant costing documents before the trial court, which had not considered the broader cost components or the effect of a contributor’s non-payment on the project and other contributors.
The contributor sought interim relief while pursuing a suit for declaration and injunction, and the developer appealed the interim orders.
issues.conclusion: The interim orders were set aside and the matter was remitted to the trial court for a fresh decision in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, interim injunctions require consideration of a prima facie case, balance of convenience and irreparable injury; the relief is equitable, and the conduct of the party seeking relief is relevant. Gujarat Bottling Co. Ltd. v. Coca Cola Co. (1995) 5 SCC 545 states these principles. In a self-financing project, an injunction affecting contributions can jeopardize the entire project and other contributors, so courts should be slow to interfere at the interim stage without considering the relevant costing material. Indore Development Authority v. Sadhana Agarwal (1995) 3 SCC 1 also addresses scrutiny of cost escalation.

rule.if: appeal_from_interim_injunction and self_financing_project and injunction_restricted_project_funding and relevant_costing_material_was_not_considered

predicates.appeal_from_interim_injunction: A party appealed an interim injunction made during a pending suit.
predicates.self_financing_project: The project depended on contributions from purchasers to fund its construction.
predicates.injunction_restricted_project_funding: The injunction limited collection of the amount sought for a unit or otherwise impeded funding of the project.
predicates.relevant_costing_material_was_not_consid: The court granting the injunction did not consider relevant cost components, supporting documents or the effect on the project and other contributors.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an interim injunction in a contribution-funded project, the injunction restricts project funding, and relevant costing material was not considered, the injunction must be set aside and the matter reconsidered.
